svg.title: DAMA core knowledge areas to FAIR principles
svg.desc: 61 proposed implementation alignments: 51 direct and 10 enabling. Eleven DAMA core knowledge areas are on the left and fifteen FAIR principles are on the right. Each ribbon has equal width; counts do not indicate strength or compliance.

path.title: Metadata Management → F1 · Direct: Assign and maintain identifiers for data and metadata resources.
Reference & Master Data Management → F1 · Direct: Maintain stable entity identifiers and mappings between identifier systems.
Data Storage & Operations → F1 · Direct: Sustain identifier services through migrations and retirement.
Data Governance → F1 · Enabling: Establish ownership and long-term commitments for identification.
Metadata Management → F2 · Direct: Capture sufficient description to discover and understand a resource.
Data Modeling & Design → F2 · Direct: Structure metadata fields and relationships for consistent interpretation.
Data Quality Management → F2 · Direct: Assess completeness and usefulness of discovery metadata.
Documents & Content Management → F2 · Direct: Apply descriptive metadata to documents and other content.
Metadata Management → F3 · Direct: Record the data identifier explicitly in its metadata.
Data Modeling & Design → F3 · Direct: Model an unambiguous relationship between metadata and the described resource.
Data Integration & Interoperability → F3 · Direct: Preserve identifiers through metadata harvesting and exchange.
Data Quality Management → F3 · Direct: Verify identifier presence and correct resource association.
Metadata Management → F4 · Direct: Register resources in searchable catalogs.
Data Integration & Interoperability → F4 · Direct: Feed and synchronize metadata with discovery services.
Documents & Content Management → F4 · Direct: Make managed content discoverable through indexed descriptions.
Data Warehousing & Business Intelligence → F4 · Direct: Register published analytical resources for discovery.
Data Integration & Interoperability → A1 · Direct: Connect identifiers to standardized retrieval interfaces.
Data Storage & Operations → A1 · Direct: Operate the services that return identified resources.
Metadata Management → A1 · Direct: Support retrieval of metadata and describe data access routes.
Data Architecture → A1 · Enabling: Define how identifiers, resolvers and retrieval services work together.
Data Integration & Interoperability → A1.1 · Direct: Implement retrieval through protocols that independent clients can implement freely.
Metadata Management → A1.1 · Direct: Expose metadata through qualifying protocols.
Data Architecture → A1.1 · Enabling: Select protocols without proprietary implementation dependencies.
Data Governance → A1.1 · Enabling: Require protocol openness in procurement and service approval.
Data Security → A1.2 · Direct: Provide identity verification and access decisions within the retrieval process.
Data Integration & Interoperability → A1.2 · Direct: Integrate protected access into data and metadata interfaces.
Metadata Management → A1.2 · Direct: Describe access conditions and the procedure for obtaining access.
Data Governance → A1.2 · Enabling: Assign decision rights for access approval and review.
Metadata Management → A2 · Direct: Retain an accessible description of withdrawn or unavailable data.
Data Storage & Operations → A2 · Direct: Preserve metadata services independently of data retention.
Documents & Content Management → A2 · Direct: Retain descriptive records when content is disposed of.
Data Governance → A2 · Enabling: Define metadata survival obligations and ownership.
Data Modeling & Design → I1 · Direct: Express meaning and relationships using an appropriate formal representation.
Metadata Management → I1 · Direct: Publish metadata in a shared, machine-interpretable representation.
Data Integration & Interoperability → I1 · Direct: Preserve meaning when exchanging representations.
Data Architecture → I1 · Enabling: Establish enterprise conventions for knowledge representation.
Reference & Master Data Management → I2 · Direct: Manage and publish reusable vocabularies and code lists as FAIR resources.
Metadata Management → I2 · Direct: Reference identified vocabulary terms in metadata.
Data Quality Management → I2 · Direct: Check actual vocabulary use and the FAIR properties of referenced vocabularies.
Data Governance → I2 · Enabling: Assign vocabulary stewardship and approval responsibilities.
Data Modeling & Design → I3 · Direct: Specify the meaning of relationships between identified resources.
Metadata Management → I3 · Direct: Record explicit, meaningful links to related resources.
Data Integration & Interoperability → I3 · Direct: Preserve and exchange qualified links across systems.
Reference & Master Data Management → I3 · Direct: Express governed identity and hierarchical relationships.
Metadata Management → R1 · Direct: Capture the context a consumer needs to assess reuse.
Data Quality Management → R1 · Direct: Validate descriptive attributes and communicate relevant quality limitations.
Data Modeling & Design → R1 · Direct: Make interpretation requirements explicit.
Data Warehousing & Business Intelligence → R1 · Direct: Explain how analytical outputs should be interpreted and reused.
Metadata Management → R1.1 · Direct: Associate each resource with an accessible licence.
Documents & Content Management → R1.1 · Direct: Publish and retain the applicable licence text and version.
Data Integration & Interoperability → R1.1 · Direct: Carry licence information with published and exchanged resources.
Data Governance → R1.1 · Enabling: Establish authority and processes for approving usage terms.
Metadata Management → R1.2 · Direct: Associate resources with their origins and processing history.
Data Integration & Interoperability → R1.2 · Direct: Capture transformations and movement between resources.
Data Warehousing & Business Intelligence → R1.2 · Direct: Explain derivation of analytical datasets and measures.
Data Storage & Operations → R1.2 · Direct: Preserve operational evidence linked to resource versions.
Data Governance → R1.3 · Enabling: Identify applicable domain standards and assign responsibility for adoption.
Data Modeling & Design → R1.3 · Direct: Implement community information models and constraints.
Metadata Management → R1.3 · Direct: Apply the relevant community metadata requirements.
Data Integration & Interoperability → R1.3 · Direct: Exchange resources according to domain standards.
Data Quality Management → R1.3 · Direct: Validate actual resources against those standards.

g.text: Source: implementation-oriented alignment in DAMA Segments High Level v1.9.0.
Each ribbon represents one proposed alignment, not strength, implementation or compliance.
